column2: alice (raw peer): 3 input streams with partial 131072-byte prefixes of declared 262144-byte payloads and no FIN, one pending 30s watch held unread on a declared-never-admitted work, one result stream requested and never read
bob's next-sequence/declare/admit/lookup/page complete within the deadline throughout the window while alice stalls

every stalled input stream is enforced at the negotiated idle/lifetime bounds (idle 5s, lifetime 30s): either the transport aborts it (observed by a failing write probe at idle+10s / lifetime+10s) or a LIMIT_EXCEEDED (code 4) Refusal naming that input stream tag is queued on the control stream and read at window end — both channels are recorded per stream in artifacts/stalls.tsv
server-group RSS: tail p90 (final 30s) <= baseline median (20-50s) + max(baseline/N, fixed slack); rust N=4 slack=64MiB, java N=2 slack=128MiB (JVM warmup allowance) — never monotonic growth
server-group FDs: tail p90 <= baseline median + 8

the abusive principal's connection sends QUIC PINGs every 5s with an explicit 60s transport idle timeout, so it outlives the silent gaps between enforcement probes; PINGs are transport traffic only and carry no object stream data. A probe that finds the connection gone with a transport idle timeout records its stream aborts as NOT attributable to the subject and does not count them

server-group write_bytes AND cancelled_write_bytes are both collected per sample and reported as rates over the window; neither is asserted against a bound here (this row's gates are progress and the RSS/FD plateaus) — they are recorded so an idle write rate can be told apart from cancelled page-cache writeback

java-server direction: heap via jstat when the JDK reports it, named gap otherwise; rust-server direction: no JVM exists, so the Java-heap scope is not applicable and the Rust heap scope is a named gap — RSS is never substituted for either
